title: Distributed Version Control
definition: A system that tracks changes in computer files and directories, allowing multiple people to work on a project simultaneously and manage differences between their versions.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine having a magical copy machine that not only makes copies of your work, but also keeps track of all the changes made to each copy. This is what distributed version control does.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Distributed version control is a software tool that lets multiple developers collaborate on a project by managing differences between their copies of the project. This allows for efficient handling of changes, merges, and conflicts.
difficulty_levels.expert: Distributed version control systems like Git enable simultaneous and independent development through the management of changes to computer files and directories. They provide robust support for branching and merging, enabling the comparison of different versions of a project and the resolution of any conflicts that arise. Distributed version control is also a cornerstone of the DevOps and agile methodologies, facilitating continuous integration and deployment.

extra_fields.insight: The conversation reveals the importance of managing versions and resolving conflicts in a distributed development environment.
